text:
lina: Quick share from the Orenda-12b quant sweep. Ran fp16 vs gptq-int8 vs a mixed-layer int4 strategy (first 8 layers fp16, rest GPTQ-int4). Dataset: 12k requests across helpdesk short prompts, multi-paragraph summaries, and code-completion slices. Headline: mixed schedule gives 60% token-cost reduction vs fp16 and preserves most longform quality; p95 slightly higher than int8 but still within our 800ms SLO for prod flows. Results + artifacts: https://go.redwood/orenda12b-mixedquant :rocket:

dan: can you paste the short table?

lina: Sure — approximate unit econ (tokens): fp16 = $0.015/token, int8 = $0.0087/token, mixed = $0.006/token. p50 latencies (ms): fp16 230, int8 185, mixed 210. p95 latencies: fp16 680, int8 740, mixed 710. Quality deltas vs fp16 (higher is better): short QA F1: int8 -0.2, mixed -0.05. Long summarization ROUGE-L: int8 -2.4, mixed -0.6. Code completion pass@1: int8 -1.6 pts, mixed -0.4 pts. Hallucination rate on citation test: int8 +1.9%, mixed +0.6%.

emil: Interesting that mixed keeps longform signal. How stable is the layer-schedule across batch sizes/hw?

lina: We tested on g5x2 and g4dn; mixed schedule is robust up to batch 12. Observed more variance at batch >16 due to memory comps. Also saw slightly higher CPU host overhead during decoding for mixed schedule because we do per-layer dequant hooks.

riley: For product routing, I'd prefer a simple heuristic that doesn't require token-length estimation. Any ideas?

dan: We tried a traffic-probabilistic router: 80% route to mixed, 20% to fp16 for safety-critical flows. For longform flows (compose/editor) we route 100% fp16. Implemented as tag-based rules in the gateway.

lina: Example gateway rule snippet we used: ```
route_rules:
  - tag: compose
    model: orenda-12b-fp16
  - tag: default
    algorithm: weighted
    variants:
      - orenda-12b-mixed: 80
      - orenda-12b-fp16: 20
```

dan: Economically that gives ~48% cost reduction vs fp16 baseline (because compose flows are small pct), with near-zero user-visible quality regression on short tasks.

emil: What about a fast rollback / graceful degrade plan?

lina: Canary plan: 3-stage. Stage A: internal canary 1% for 24h with full eval logging. Stage B: 10% external for 48h with shadow fp16 requests for sampled longform keys. Stage C: 50% if metrics OK. Pass criteria: no >0.4% drop in short QA F1, <0.8 ROUGE-L drop, p95 latency <800ms. If hallucination on citation slice increases by >1.0% we auto-roll back that tag.

ops-bot: rolloutbot: Scheduled canary: orenda-12b-mixed -> 2026-03-22T04:30Z at 1% (internal).

riley: Two asks before canary: (1) add the citation priming slice (2) instrument per-variant token-cost and token-count signals in the console dashboard so finance can reconcile.

lina: On it. I'll queue a 5k-turn citation priming eval tonight and add metrics to the console dashboard (cost by variant, tokens/resp distribution).

emil: One more note — mixed schedule increases model artifact complexity (we need separate kernels + provenance). Let's add a model-tagging field and ensure private deploys get the artifact bundle.

dan: Agreed. Add model tag: orenda-12b-mixed-sched-v1 and include provenance JSON in the release bundle.

lina: Final recommendation: adopt mixed-layer quant schedule as default for latency-sensitive public routes, route compose/editor to fp16, canary as above, and require artifact + provenance for Dedicated/Private. We'll reconvene after citation slice results.
